candidates.title: Cache-Aware Joint Router Adaptation for Memory-Efficient MoE Inference
candidates.reason: Directly targets memory-constrained MoE inference by adapting routing to expert-cache state. The primary-source abstract reports higher expert-cache hit rate and substantially lower expert-weight traffic on Qwen3 and GPT-OSS, making it highly relevant to expert caching, prefetching, and CPU/GPU offload research.

candidates.title: PCoMoE: Shifting MoE Inference from Monolithic Expert Selection to Fine-Grained Path Composition
candidates.reason: Reframes MoE execution below the whole-expert abstraction using fine-grained path composition, compatibility-aware pruning, and a hardware-friendly execution engine. The primary-source abstract reports up to 1.31x end-to-end inference speedup and released code, making it a strong systems candidate distinct from ordinary expert placement or cache management.

candidates.title: ACE: Adaptive Calibration-Free Expert Skipping for MoE-based LLMs
candidates.reason: Provides training-free, calibration-free token-adaptive expert skipping with offline expert statistics and lightweight runtime decisions. It directly reduces routed-expert computation and is useful for comparing compute-side MoE reduction against memory/offload-oriented approaches already emphasized by the repository.

candidates.title: Training-Free Halving of Activated Experts in Fine-Grained Mixture-of-Experts Models
candidates.reason: Shows a parameter-free inference-time method for halving activated experts while preserving a reference router-probability mass. The primary-source abstract reports only small accuracy loss on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B while halving routed-expert compute, providing a simple but potentially important MoE inference baseline.

discovery_stats.query_summary: Rotated away from the two recent high-duplicate broad system-search rounds and screened September 2026 primary-source MoE inference papers. Four strong candidates spanning cache-aware routing, path-compositional execution, adaptive expert skipping, and inference-time expert-count reduction passed lightweight relevance and repository dedupe checks.
